title: Converbs I: after, before, without, until
intro: This unit links actions in time. Where English puts a word such as **after** or **until** in front of a clause, Turkmen puts a suffix on its verb: *Öýe gelenden soň jaň ederin* (I'll call after I get home), *Ýatmazdan öň kitap okaýaryn* (I read before going to bed), *Ol hiç zat diýmän gitdi* (she left without saying anything), *Ol gelýänçä garaşaýyn* (let me wait until he comes), *Bu ýere geleli bäri* (since I came here). These forms are called converbs. As with `-AndA` and `-(Y)p` ([A2 unit 11](a2-u11)), the clause with the converb comes first, and only the last verb shows the tense and the person.

blocks.text: You know *soň* after a noun in the ablative ([A2 unit 9](a2-u09)): *işden soň* (after work), *sapakdan soň* (after the lesson), *iki günden soň* (in two days). To say **after (someone) does something**, the verb takes `-An` and the same ablative, then *soň*: *gel-* → *gelen* → *gelenden soň*, after (someone) comes or came. It is `-AndA` ([A2 unit 11](a2-u11)) with *-dan* in place of *-da*.

The spelling is that of `-AndA`. After a vowel `-An` is just *-n*: *okandan*. A final *e* becomes *ä*: *işländen*. The verbs that soften *t* before a vowel soften it here too: *gidenden*, *edenden*, *aýdandan*.

**No tense of its own.** The verb at the end says when: *Öýe gelenden soň, jaň ederin*, I'll call after I get home; *Öýe gelenden soň, jaň etdim*, I called after I got home. **Who?** When both actions are yours, say the subject once, at the start or not at all. The two halves can also have different subjects, each said before its verb: *Sapak gutarandan soň, men bazara gitjek* (when the lesson is over, I'm going to the bazaar).

items.tk: Öýe gelenden soň, saňa jaň ederin.
items.seg: Öý|e gel|en|den soň, saňa jaň ed|er|in.
items.en: I'll call you after I get home.
After eating, we had tea.

items.tk: Sapak gutarandan soň, men bazara gitjek.
items.seg: Sapak gutar|an|dan soň, men bazar|a git|jek.
items.en: When the lesson is over, I'm going to the bazaar.

items.tk: Işini gutarandan soň, Merdan öýe gaýtdy.
items.seg: Iş|i|ni gutar|an|dan soň, Merdan öý|e gaýt|dy.
items.en: After finishing his work, Merdan went home.
Give me the book when you've read it.

blocks.title: My, your: two ways to say who
blocks.text: Like `-AndA`, `-An` can take the endings of **my** and **your** before *-dan*: *gelenimden soň*, after I came; *geleniňden soň*, after you came. This course practises the plain form with the subject said, and accepts both. In stories you will also meet a short form written as one word, *gelensoň* for *gelenden soň*.

blocks.title: When or after?
blocks.text: *Öýe gelende* is **when I get home**, at that moment; *öýe gelenden soň* is **after I've got home**. And keep the tense for the last verb: *gelenden soň*, not `geldiden soň` or `gelýänden soň`.

**Before** works the same way with *öň*. After a noun in the ablative: *sapakdan öň* (before the lesson), *nahardan öň* (before the meal). After a verb, the suffix is `-mAzdAn`: *ýat-* → *ýatmazdan öň*, before going to bed; *gel-* → *gelmezden öň*, before (someone) comes.

The *-mAz* in it is the one of *gelmez*, he won't come ([A2 unit 4](a2-u04)), but here it makes nothing negative: *Ýatmazdan öň kitap okaýaryn* means I read **before** going to bed, and then I do go to bed. Read it as **before (I) have not yet gone to bed**. A consonant follows the stem, so there is no *e* → *ä* and no soft *t*: *işlemezden*, *gitmezden*.

items.en: I read before going to bed.
I wash my hands before eating.

items.tk: Ýola çykmazdan öň, maňa jaň et.
items.seg: Ýol|a çyk|mazdan öň, maňa jaň et.
items.en: Call me before you set off.
We cleaned the house before the guests came.

items.tk: Bir zady bilmezden öň aýtmak bolmaz.
items.seg: Bir zad|y bil|mezden öň aýt|mak bol|maz.
items.en: You shouldn't talk about a thing before you know it.

blocks.title: Before, not not
blocks.text: *Gelmezden öň* is **before (someone) comes**, never **before (someone) doesn't come**. The shape is fixed, `-mAzdAn`, with *-z*: *ýatmazdan öň*, not `ýatmandan öň`. And there is no `-Andan öň`: *ýatandan soň* is **after**, *ýatmazdan öň* is **before**.

blocks.title: The clause comes first
blocks.text: English can put **before** at either end: **I read before I go to bed**, **Before I go to bed, I read**. Turkmen puts the clause with `-mAzdAn öň` first, as it does with every converb in this unit.

`-mAn` is the negative of `-(Y)p` ([A2 unit 11](a2-u11)). Where *-(Y)p* joins an action that happens, *-mAn* joins one that doesn't, and English usually says **without …ing**: *Ol hiç zat diýmän gitdi* (she left without saying anything), *Men nahar iýmän işe gitdim* (I went to work without eating).

It is the negative *-mA* with *-n*. Before that *n*, *-me* becomes *-mä*: *gelmän*, *iýmän*, *işlemän*; with back vowels the suffix is *-man*: *okaman*, *ýatman*. You have met the same *-mAn* inside *gelmändi* and *gelmändir* ([B1 unit 1](b1-u01), [B1 unit 3](b1-u03)).

items.en: She left without saying anything.
I went to work without eating.
We studied all night without sleeping.
He left without saying goodbye.

items.tk: Bagyşla, men bilmän seniň ruçkaňy aldym.
items.seg: Bagyşla, men bil|mä|n seniň ruçka|ň|y al|dy|m.
items.en: Sorry, I took your pen by mistake.

blocks.title: Without or before?
blocks.text: *Nahar iýmän işe gitdim*: I went to work **without** eating; I never ate. *Nahar iýmezden öň elimi ýuwdum*: I washed my hands **before** eating; then I ate.

blocks.title: One letter makes the difference
blocks.text: *Hoşlaşyp gitdi*: he said goodbye and left. *Hoşlaşman gitdi*: he left **without** saying goodbye. The vowel follows the verb: *hoşlaşman*, but *gelmän*, never `hoşlaşmän`.

To say **until (something) happens**, add `-ýAnçA` to the verb stem: *gel-* → *gelýänçä*, until (someone) comes; *gutar-* → *gutarýança*, until (something) ends; *oka-* → *okaýança*. The first part is the *-ýAn* of *gelýän* ([B1 unit 5](b1-u05)), so stems behave as they do before `-ýAr`: *gidýänçä*, *edýänçä*, and an *e* stays *e*: *işleýänçä*.

**Who?** `-ýAnçA` takes the short endings of the past ([A2 unit 1](a2-u01)): *-m* for **I**, *-ň* for **you**, *-k* for **we**, *-ňYz* for **you** (plural or polite), and nothing for **he, she, it** and **they**. The pronoun in front is optional: *(Men) gelýänçäm, şu ýerde garaş*, wait here until I come.

blocks.title: *gelmek*: until I come, until you come…

rows.en: until he, she or it comes (also gelýänçe)

blocks.text: With back vowels the suffix is *-ýança*: *dolanýançam*, until I come back; *gutarýança*. For **he** and **she** you will also see *gelýänçe*, with *e*; both are correct. Like the other converbs, `-ýAnçA` has no tense: the last verb gives it.

items.en: Wait here until I come.
Let me wait until he comes.
We sat in the café until the rain stopped.
I slept all the way from Ashgabat to Mary.
Goodbye until we meet again!

blocks.title: By the time, and tä
blocks.text: When the last verb tells what was already over, `-ýAnçA` reads as **by the time**: *Biz wokzala barýançak, otly gidipdi* (by the time we got to the station, the train had left). And *tä* in front stresses **right up until**: *Tä men gelýänçäm garaş* (wait for me, right until I'm back).

blocks.title: Until with a noun, until with a verb
blocks.text: With a noun, **until** is *çenli* ([A1 unit 7](a1-u07)): *agşama çenli*, until the evening. With a verb, use `-ýAnçA`: *ol gelýänçä*, until he comes. And don't mix it up with `-AndA`: *ol gelende* is **when he comes**.

You know *bäri* after a time in the ablative ([A2 unit 9](a2-u09)): *irden bäri* (since the morning), *köp ýyldan bäri* (for many years). After a verb, *bäri* follows `-(A)lY`: *gel-* → *geleli bäri*, since (someone) came; *göç-* → *göçeli bäri*, since (someone) moved; *başla-* → *başlaly bäri*, since (something) began.

The shape is that of **let's** for two people ([A2 unit 7](a2-u07)): *geleli*, *gideli*, *okaly*, with *e* → *ä* (*işläli*) and the soft *t* (*gideli*). Only *bäri* after it makes it **since**: *Geleli!* is **let's come**, *geleli bäri* is **since (someone) came**.

As after *irden bäri*, the last verb is in the present for something that still goes on, where English says **have been**: *Aşgabada göçeli bäri, şäheriň merkezinde ýaşaýarys* (since moving to Ashgabat, we've been living in the city centre). With the past, it tells what has happened since then: *Ol gideli bäri, oňa iki gezek jaň etdim* (since she left, I've called her twice). **Who?** Say the subject at the start; `-(A)lY bäri` takes no ending.

items.tk: Bu ýere geleli bäri, her gün türkmençe gürleýärin.
items.seg: Bu ýer|e gel|eli bäri, her gün türkmençe gürle|ýär|in.
items.en: Since coming here, I've been speaking Turkmen every day.

items.seg: Aşgabad|a göç|eli bäri, köp adam bilen tanyş|dy|m.
items.en: Since moving to Ashgabat, I've got to know a lot of people.

items.tk: Okuwymy gutaraly bäri, kakamyň ýanynda işleýärin.
items.seg: Okuw|ym|y gutar|aly bäri, kaka|m|yň ýan|y|n|da işle|ýär|in.
items.en: Since finishing my studies, I've been working with my father.

items.tk: Biz tanyşaly bäri, ol meniň iň gowy dostum.
items.seg: Biz tanyş|aly bäri, ol meniň iň gowy dost|um.
items.en: Since we met, she has been my best friend.

items.seg: Ol gid|eli bäri, oňa iki gezek jaň et|di|m.
items.en: Since she left, I've called her twice.

blocks.title: Since, not let's
blocks.text: *Geleli bäri* needs *bäri*: without it, *geleli* is **let's come**. *Bäri* comes after the verb, never before it. And in writing you may also meet `-AnY bäri` in the same sense (*bolany bäri*, since it became); this course practises `-(A)lY bäri`.

lines.tk: Gaty gowy! Ýola çykmazdan öň, Köneürgenç barada köp okadym.
lines.en: Really well! Before setting off, I read a lot about Köneürgenç.

lines.tk: Ol ýere barandan soň näme etdiň?
lines.en: What did you do after you got there?

lines.tk: Hiç ýerde durman, göni minara gitdim. Ýadaýançam gezdim.
lines.en: I went straight to the minaret without stopping anywhere. I walked around until I was tired.

lines.tk: Gaýdyp geleli bäri, diňe Köneürgenç barada gürleýärsiň!
lines.en: Since you came back, you've talked about nothing but Köneürgenç!

lines.tk: Sen hem bir gezek bar. Ýöne ýola çykmazdan öň, maňa jaň et!
lines.en: You should go once too. But call me before you set off!

summary: A converb goes on the first verb; only the last verb shows the tense and the person.
**After**: `-An` + *-dAn soň*: *gelenden soň*, *okandan soň*, *işländen soň*. With a noun: *işden soň*.
**Before**: `-mAzdAn öň`: *ýatmazdan öň*, *işlemezden öň*. It looks negative but isn't.
**Until**: `-ýAnçA` with the short endings *-m, -ň, -k, -ňYz*: *gelýänçäm*, *gelýänçäň*, *gelýänçä*. With a noun: *çenli*.
**Since**: `-(A)lY bäri`, shaped like **let's**: *geleli bäri*, *göçeli bäri*; the present for what still goes on.
